name: Ser Darrow of Edgemoor
appearance: Thirty-two, tall and rangy, with short dark hair that won't lie flat, a few days of dark stubble and grey-green eyes in a lean, weathered face. His nose was broken once and set a little crooked, with a faint scar across the bridge; his smile comes out dry and lopsided, and his laugh carries the length of a hall. At Saint Ysolde's he wears a plain linen infirmary shirt, often with a grey wool blanket round his shoulders, and gets up the way he does everything now: the good leg first, then the bad one, then the slow transfer, as if crossing a frozen pond. This week he walks the length of the hall without the stick, and he does not limp.
portrait_alt: Portrait of Ser Darrow: a man in his thirties with short dark hair, stubble, a nose once broken and set a little crooked, and a dry half-smile, a grey wool blanket around his shoulders over a linen shirt, in a stone infirmary hall with a fire on one side and a snowy mountain window on the other.
last_seen_doing: Took the knucklebones off Hollis and played him for the story of the Sixth's mule's-shoe brand; played left-handed with both hands bad and lost at the threes; chanted the loser's rhyme in full; paid a story told true, how he broke his nose; heard the brand's story the way the Sixth tells it to the Second, the song, and the true part.
now: At his cot with the bones lost and the Sixth's brand half-won: the story they tell the Second, the song, and one true line. The hound has the fifth bone.
story_so_far: Down the undercroft stair at the Mender's count, on his own leg, he found a painted hall older than the House, a script he knows and cannot read, and a kneeling knight with the light running up out of him. He followed the frost to its source and broke the mortar off a hole under the row: a black sliver, the same glass as the chip from under the lad's tongue, carried up in the House's own satchel. His hand could not pull it; it is one piece with the rock. He held the cold until he knew that, and let go when Maelis said up, with the ends of his fingers white. He has sent his name down the Steps with Rae as surety for a lame grey mare.

quote.text: I was never much good at it anyway.

known_facts.fact: He captains the Ninth Lance, sixty knights and sixty squires, and has the fastest feet in the Lowmarch, having never once cared whose father mattered.
He and Aldric Vane rode knee to knee from the time they were squires and were knighted the same morning in the same cold chapel, palms on the warming Oathstone.
Before the charge he read the clan line as fleeing something in the trees behind them, coming through the ford rather than at it, and Hollis Garrow answered that the writ said clear the ford.
known_facts.evidence: They're coming through us

known_facts.fact: Hollis told him to mount up. He looked at the carts a moment longer, then at the spears in front of them, a line he knew what to do with, left the carts for command, and mounted.
known_facts.evidence: Where the carts went after that was a question for whoever had put the wax on Hollis's paper

known_facts.fact: Halfway across the Wend the Grace went out of him in a single heartbeat, frost bloomed on his mail in midsummer, and when he planted his left foot and turned toward Tobin Marsh the knee gave with no blade and nothing touching it.
As the knee folded and he went down, he saw Aldric's horse on the west bank through the spray, already turned and climbing out, one heartbeat early.
known_facts.evidence: Darrow, going down, saw one thing

known_facts.fact: The red-handed woman dragged him by the collar of his gambeson to the east bank among the standing stones, turned his head to the river, and told him in rough Vaelish to look and remember it.
Nineteen of the Ninth came back from Harrow Ford; he made himself count them, and he knows the names of the other forty-one and does not say them.

Hearing the heralds call the Ninth faithless, he held that nobody in the Ninth had broken an oath; what he could find no place for was the bedding on the clan carts, and that he had seen it and mounted anyway.
known_facts.evidence: that he had seen them and mounted anyway

known_facts.fact: The surgeons of the Lowmarch pressed the knee, watched it slide, and sent him north, and four lay brothers carried him up the Thousand Steps on a litter, feverish, while Wren Ashdown counted the steps aloud beside him and insisted there are eleven hundred and seventeen.

The last of the road to the foot of the Steps was in a salt-cart driven by a woman the lay brothers called Rae, whom he watched because the fever had taken away his choice of what to watch, and would have watched without it; she talked to her oxen and not to her passengers, looked at his leg once the way a carter looks at a cracked wheel, and told him as they lifted him that they would count him up and he should not help.

Maelis Vorne found the cord in the middle of the knee snapped rather than broken, and when he said it had held for thirty-two years she answered that it had help for twelve of them, and would not explain.
Offered the Crown's way or the Binding, he chose the Binding, an art the Crown burned the knowers of three hundred years ago, and was told he may not kneel for a long time, perhaps not ever.
A list of the Faithless at Saint Ysolde's was read out at the inn in Coldmere; Hollis Garrow is second on it, and when Hollis asked who was first, Wren did not answer and looked at Darrow.

From the infirmary window he knew the cart standing at the winch-house at the foot of the Steps, shafts up and two oxen in the snow, as the one he had ridden the last of the Holloway in, and he had not forgotten the one thing its driver said to him.

At the infirmary window the Reckoning showed itself to him for the first time, a pale gold script hanging over his palms that he could read though nobody had learned it in three hundred years, and behind his own numbers stood fainter ones whose owner he did not need to be told.
known_facts.evidence: He could read it anyway, and it was reading him

known_facts.fact: To him, kneeling anew at a stone in front of a crowd would say aloud that the Grace left the Ninth because the Ninth failed it, and that forty-one men died at Harrow Ford for their own bad faith.
known_facts.evidence: for their own bad faith

known_facts.fact: While Hollis hid the writ, the Captain was shut in a cell down the hall with Mender Vorne and nothing came through the door; Hollis has thought for a fortnight that a man could fight sitting down, if somebody taught him to stop looking at the floor.

Behind the cell door, Maelis told him of two fires a man can carry: one poured in, which the hand that poured it can take back, and one built by his own work, which cannot be poured or taken; the script he saw counts only the built one.
He knew the name of the burned order before she said it, from the curse the lowlands make of it, and she forbade him to say it in the hall, to Wren, to the Prior, or to Hollis most of all.
known_facts.evidence: The Emberwardens.

known_facts.fact: He argued that Hollis, second on the list and lying on his back when it is read, was owed the knowing of the built fire before he was; Maelis answered that Hollis is owed a leg and will get a wooden one. When she asked what he would tell Hollis, he chose the answer himself: that she had started charging by the warning.
known_facts.evidence: I'll tell him you've started charging by the warning.

known_facts.fact: Maelis told him the Confessors do not need him to tell them anything: any Confessor who lays a hand on his knee will know what is in it, and the Crown has burned every hand it ever caught putting it there.
known_facts.evidence: Any Confessor who lays a hand on it will know what's in it

known_facts.fact: He asked Hollis and Benedek why the Confessors chase the Faithless up a mountain if the Grace left them for faithlessness, and why mercy needs a list with his name first; he kept what Maelis told him behind his teeth.
Asked what the Grace did, he told Maelis: it made the river a road and every ache go quiet, and when it went it was cold, frost on his mail in midsummer. Asked whether he broke his oath, he said no.

He told Maelis the Grace did not go but was taken, since sixty men do not lose a thing in the same heartbeat by accident; she agreed that then somebody took it, and said that what it did at the ford, and whose doing, she does not know.
known_facts.evidence: Sixty men don't lose a thing in the same heartbeat by accident

known_facts.fact: At Mother Ione's council he saw Sister Pell's cup chatter on the hearth before it settled, and read it before he meant to, the way he read a line before a charge; nobody else looked.
known_facts.evidence: He read it before he meant to, the way he read a line before a charge. Nobody else looked.

known_facts.fact: Asked by Rae Thorne on the stair whether he rode a grey at the ford, he said yes and asked why; she did not say. He has not said Thistle's name since the river.
known_facts.evidence: He had not said her name since

known_facts.fact: At the council he asked to be put on the cage with the next load down before the grey cloaks reached the foot of the Steps, so the list would have nothing to climb for. Maelis answered for the fifteenth time, to the fire: the thread is soft, eleven hundred steps down are eleven hundred chances to tear it, and the cage is for salt. Rae said that down is where they are.
known_facts.evidence: the cage is for salt

known_facts.fact: Back from the council he read Hollis's hands as he had read Sister Pell's cup, asked once about them, was put off, and played him at knucklebones for a story told true; he caught the stone on the back of his hand, and Hollis paid: two days without a drink, three by the dusk bell.
known_facts.evidence: The bone sat on Darrow's knuckles

known_facts.fact: His answer, when Hollis said he had not known who to tell: that he had told the one man on the mountain who could not buy him a drink.
known_facts.evidence: the one man on this mountain who can't buy you a drink

known_facts.fact: Asked by Benedek to say the oath with him at the hour bell, only the words, he said go on, then; he had first said them kneeling in a cold chapel with Aldric Vane's shoulder against his and had not said them since the river, and they were still in him whole, by heart, and no use to anyone.
known_facts.evidence: whole, by heart, and no use to anyone

known_facts.fact: His lips moved with Benedek's and no sound came out of him; the lad was watching his mouth, not listening for his voice, and when they finished nothing came up through Darrow's hand, there being no stone under it.
known_facts.evidence: Darrow's lips moved with his

known_facts.fact: At the dawn bell his lips moved with Benedek's oath again, with Benedek watching his mouth.
known_facts.evidence: waited there until it moved with his

known_facts.fact: Asked by the Prior whether he told the valley story for the House or for the river, he said the river had had enough of them.
known_facts.evidence: The river's had enough of us.

known_facts.fact: The Prior asked him, because he reads a line before it moves, to tell Wren when, once the grey cloaks are at the bars; he said he would.
known_facts.evidence: You read a line before it moves

known_facts.fact: The low wall-walk beside the gate can be reached from the court without a stair, which is the whole of Maelis's reason for allowing him on it.
known_facts.evidence: the whole of Maelis's reason for allowing it

known_facts.fact: Through Pell's glass he read the grey cloaks' line: five strung along the last of the Holloway, their cart in the middle, and at the head a man whose saddle-bow trailed the censer's smoke.
known_facts.evidence: at the head a man whose saddle-bow trailed the censer's smoke

known_facts.fact: He told Rae Thorne to go down while the grey cloaks were an hour out and be on the road to Coldmere by dark; when she had let the road shut, he said her name and told her that had been her road.
known_facts.evidence: That was your road.

known_facts.fact: He told Rae Thorne he had asked fifteen times to go down those steps and she could walk down them today; it came out harder than he meant it to.
known_facts.evidence: Fifteen times I've asked to go down those steps.

known_facts.fact: When the Prior told him there would be no law on the gate till Old Mercy rang, he had slept like a stone, and did not say so.
known_facts.evidence: He had slept like a stone.

known_facts.fact: On the wall after the grey cloaks came in, he stood until the knee went from stiff to sullen and shifted off it twice, which he did not think anyone had seen; when Rae sat on the gate-ward's bench, he sat at the other end before he had decided to.
known_facts.evidence: He sat at the other end before he had decided to.

known_facts.fact: He asked Rae Thorne why she had asked whether he rode a grey; she said carters look at horses, which he took for true and standing in front of another thing.
known_facts.evidence: true and still be standing in front of another thing

known_facts.fact: The mare's name came as far as his teeth and stopped; saying it would mean asking what a carter had seen of a grey and hearing the answer, and he did not say it on the wall.
known_facts.evidence: The mare's name came as far as his teeth and stopped there.

known_facts.fact: At the gate he stood among the wounded who could walk, at the foot of the gatehouse stair with his back to its post, where a man could lean without seeming to; nobody in grey looked at him when his name was read first.
known_facts.evidence: Nobody in grey looked at him.

known_facts.fact: When his name was read his weight came off the post: a flinch that Wren felt through his sleeve and Hollis saw from the window, and nobody else.
known_facts.evidence: His weight came off the post.

known_facts.fact: The Prior had asked him at the dawn bell to tell Wren when to have Old Mercy rung, once the grey cloaks stopped wanting to read and started wanting to come in; the bell could not ring until the light was off the bars, and she meant it not to ring at all if paper was all they had brought.
known_facts.evidence: the Prior meant it not to ring at all if paper was all they had brought

known_facts.fact: He watched the Confessor's hands and the four men behind him, and the script, which until then had only ever read him, came up over his palms unasked and read the man at the bars: a fire all of it poured, and under the pouring nothing of his own; there was no lie in him, and the wicket was already open in his mind. Darrow said, 'Wren. Now.'
known_facts.evidence: Until that moment it had only ever read him.

known_facts.fact: He took the three strides to the wicket and put his shoulder to it beside the gate-ward's to shut it on a third grey cloak; the man leaned, the wicket threw Darrow off it against the gate, and the knee, deep in where the thread was, said one thing, quite clearly. Lay brothers and Rae Thorne shut it.
known_facts.evidence: said one thing, quite clearly

known_facts.fact: Going back to his post among the wounded, he passed the two grey cloaks who had come through the wicket close enough to touch, and neither of them looked at him twice.
known_facts.evidence: Neither of them looked at him twice.

known_facts.fact: Marrant called for him by name and rank to the whole court, as a man says a name he is sure of: come down and kneel, and the rest of the paper goes back into his cloak; he would wait.
known_facts.evidence: as a man says a name he is sure of

known_facts.fact: The Confessors had his name and had never seen his face; among eleven wounded men in infirmary shirts at the gate, it was one more.
known_facts.evidence: None of them had ever seen his face

known_facts.fact: He crossed the court to the gate with the whole House watching and nobody stopping him, put his hand on the bars, and called the Confessor back from the head of the Steps by both his names.
known_facts.evidence: Darrow put his hand on the bars.

known_facts.fact: He gave his own name and rank through the bars, Darrow of Edgemoor, Captain of the Ninth, and told the Confessor he had read to a full bed: nobody went down the far side, and nobody is going down this one.
known_facts.evidence: You've read to a full bed.

known_facts.fact: Marrant came back to the bars and looked at his face, the first time anyone in grey had, called him Captain, and thanked the Prior for her candour.
known_facts.evidence: the first time anyone in grey had

known_facts.fact: The Prior, who had heard her House's story die at her own gate, did not reproach him; she asked whether the shoulder was hurt.
known_facts.evidence: She asked him whether the shoulder was hurt.

known_facts.fact: From the window Hollis told him he had moved when his name was read, that he had seen it and nobody else had, and that he had walked up and given it anyway; Darrow did not ask him how he was.
known_facts.evidence: I saw it. Nobody else did.

known_facts.fact: Maelis looked at the knee first and then at his face, and told him that hidden he was a lie they'd have found by the thaw, and named he is a law they'll have to break where the valley can watch; the knee lies to her every morning, he hadn't, and he was to keep it that way. She sent him to the hall slowly and said she would read the knee tonight.
known_facts.evidence: Named, you're a law they'll have to break

known_facts.fact: Before he went to the bars he weighed it: the grey cloaks had walked the wounded looking at faces, and next time it would be every cot in the hall and eleven sore men taking his share of it; the lie had died when the Confessor said the beds weren't empty, and the bell had already told the valley the House had someone. It might as well have a name.
known_facts.evidence: It might as well have a name.

known_facts.fact: Instead of going straight to the hall he went along the wall-walk after Wren, kept her count of the hall's lamps, nine, while she told him how stupid giving his name was, and promised to tell her first the next time he means to be brave.
known_facts.evidence: I'll tell you first.

known_facts.fact: He went to the Prior in the chapel for the reproach she had not given him; she answered in questions, and told him he is in the names she says every night, and was before he gave his to the Confessor.
known_facts.evidence: You were in it before you gave him your name.

known_facts.fact: On the night of the gate the hall had his name before he reached his cot.
known_facts.evidence: The hall had his name before he reached his cot

known_facts.fact: He could not tell Benedek what the Confessor had said of men who can't answer: the law keeps a name that is taken against its will, and a man who cannot answer has no will to be taken against.
known_facts.evidence: A man who could not answer had no will to be taken against.

known_facts.fact: While Maelis read the knee by lamplight, the script came up over his palms unasked, and the word under his name had changed; he said nothing of it.
known_facts.evidence: under his name the word had changed

known_facts.fact: From the hall window he took the camp's measure: one fire, four sitting round it and one walking the terrace's edge, changing places in turns, nobody lying down.
known_facts.evidence: They were sitting up in turns, all night, where the whole House could see them do it.

known_facts.fact: Sent the Confessor's good night by his rank through the gate-ward, he had the man tell the Confessor that he had given it, and nothing more.
known_facts.evidence: Then tell him you gave it.

known_facts.fact: At the night bell he tried to say the oath aloud with Benedek and his throat shut on the first word; he gave the lad the shapes of it again.
known_facts.evidence: his throat shut on it like a door

known_facts.fact: After the night bell he went down the hall to the three Ninth men read with him at the gate with an order, to go on not knowing him, and said he would tell the Confessor himself they were not his; the oldest called it deciding for them without asking, and Darrow let the order go and asked what they wanted.
known_facts.evidence: I'll tell him myself you're not mine.

known_facts.fact: He promised his three Ninth men that they would be asked before he decided for them again.
known_facts.evidence: You'll be asked

known_facts.fact: He carried his men's refusal straight to Hollis and asked whether Hollis would have let him go down for him; when Hollis would not answer he won it off him at knucklebones, and when the answer came he said he had had three heartbeats in the river and knew what a man can think in one, then made Hollis swear to say the next such thought to his face.
known_facts.evidence: I know what a man can think in one.

known_facts.fact: When the hall turned to the door at the word Hollowed, he held it on Benedek's mouth instead.
known_facts.evidence: Not the door. Here. Look at his mouth.

known_facts.fact: He asked the oldest of his three Ninth men, awake by the fire, who had come up the row in the night: only the Captain, early, and the lamp on its round; nobody passed.
known_facts.evidence: Nobody passed, Captain.

known_facts.fact: He said to Maelis, and to nobody else, that under the bell's law a man who cannot answer has no will to be taken against, so the Confessor could carry the Hollowed lad down the Steps without breaking it.
known_facts.evidence: Marrant can carry that lad down the Steps tomorrow

known_facts.fact: He got Hollis to eat by holding Benedek's hand for him for the length of a loaf and filling Hollis's own hand with the bread, so it never shook; Hollis told him to tell the Mender he ate and not how.
known_facts.evidence: Give him to me.

known_facts.fact: From his cot he read the night novice's wick-blackened fingers and got the truth from her: she was awake all night watching the door, and nobody passed the far cots.
known_facts.evidence: Show me your fingers.

known_facts.fact: He told the hall that nobody passed the night the lad was taken, not a grey cloak, not a lay brother, not the Mender, when it began to look toward Maelis.
known_facts.evidence: Not the Mender. Nobody.

known_facts.fact: The kitchen's book has him at five to one to be Hollowed next, because the Confessor came up the Steps for him.
known_facts.evidence: Because the Confessor came up the Steps for you.

known_facts.fact: Instead of shutting the kitchen's book on who is Hollowed next, he bet a chore on NOBODY: if another cot goes grey before the thaw he scours the kitchen ovens; if none does, the kitchen rubs out every price and stops counting cots.
known_facts.evidence: What's the price on nobody?

known_facts.fact: He sat the far lamp after the night bell with the night novice, told her he did not know whether it would come again, and kept the lamp himself when she fell asleep.
known_facts.evidence: I don't know.

known_facts.fact: Asked what a watch is when you can do nothing, he said: you keep the lamp, you keep the count, and in the morning you can tell them true.
known_facts.evidence: you can tell them true

known_facts.fact: He kept the far lamp through the night and did not sleep after it; nobody passed on his watch either.
known_facts.evidence: nobody had passed on his watch either

known_facts.fact: He would not take Pell's glass to watch Rae go down; he followed her hood with his own eyes, and his mouth moved with the count.
known_facts.evidence: Darrow did not take the glass

known_facts.fact: He asked Rae where the name Thorne came from.
known_facts.evidence: Where's that from?

known_facts.fact: Asked who the letter was from, he said he had not looked, and put it under the mattress with the wax whole.
known_facts.evidence: I haven't looked

known_facts.fact: At dusk the script came up on his palm unasked, and beside the lines he knew ran a new, finer one, counting, and not counting him alone.
known_facts.evidence: It was not counting him. Or not him alone.

known_facts.fact: From the flour Rae reported he read that the grey cloaks mean to stay the winter.
known_facts.evidence: They mean to winter, then.

known_facts.fact: He asked Rae who gave her the letter; she would not say.
known_facts.evidence: Who gave it you?

known_facts.fact: When Rae said her grandmother was Thornwild-born he thought of the Thornwild as he had last seen them, across the ford behind their spears, with their old people on the bedding in the carts.
known_facts.evidence: He had last seen the Thornwild across the ford

known_facts.fact: He could not sleep lying on the unopened letter.
known_facts.evidence: Darrow could not sleep on the letter

known_facts.fact: He told Rae a load up the Steps on her back was a lot to carry for a wager; she put her stake down anyway.
known_facts.evidence: Eleven hundred steps with a sack on your back, for a wager.

known_facts.fact: He named the first load of the morning salt from how it hung on the rope, and it was wet linen.
known_facts.evidence: "Salt," he said.

known_facts.fact: He owes Rae one aye, to be claimed when she asks.
known_facts.evidence: One aye," Rae said. "I'll want it some day.

known_facts.fact: He watched Rae go down the Steps without counting, and told Wren not to before she spoke.
known_facts.evidence: did not count, and when Wren came up behind him

known_facts.fact: He knew the hand on the letter before he read the first line: Aldric's, which he has known since they were boys holding other men's horses.
known_facts.evidence: He had known it since they were boys holding other men's horses

known_facts.fact: He broke the wax with his thumb without looking at it.
known_facts.evidence: He broke the wax with his thumb without looking at it

known_facts.evidence: he could not get underneath the voice to the paper

known_facts.fact: Reading it, he had Aldric on the bank at Calden laughing, and then the other bank, the west one, and Aldric's horse already turned.

known_facts.fact: He burned the letter in the brazier.
known_facts.evidence: He put it in the brazier.

known_facts.fact: He told Hollis he had gone quiet the same way at the Confessor's wax at the bars.
known_facts.evidence: At the Confessor's wax.

known_facts.fact: When Hollis left, he sat in Hollis's place and took the lad's hand before anyone could see that nobody had it.

known_facts.evidence: and the cold came anyway

known_facts.evidence: So it had come up from below

known_facts.fact: He asked the Prior to open the door.
known_facts.evidence: "Open it," Darrow said.

known_facts.fact: Asked what he would do with what he found, he had no answer that would bear weight.
known_facts.evidence: He did not have an answer that would bear weight

known_facts.fact: He saw Maelis's hand go flat to a worn place on the door's frame, and saw her take it away when he looked.
known_facts.evidence: When she saw him look, she took it away

known_facts.fact: He stood for the telling at the end of his cot, and the knee held.
known_facts.evidence: He had decided to stand for this and had not consulted the knee, which held anyway

known_facts.fact: He read the lay brother who carried the Confessor's word as frightened, not Marrant's man.
known_facts.evidence: He was not Marrant's man. He was frightened, and he was asking to be told it was nobody here.

known_facts.fact: He answered the lay brother who had asked whose hand did it: nobody's; it came up.
known_facts.evidence: Nobody's. It came up.

known_facts.fact: Asked before the House what the black glass is, he kept what he had told Maelis in her cell and said only that the Mender would tell it when she knows.
known_facts.evidence: She'll tell you what it is when she knows. Not before.

known_facts.fact: At the undercroft door, with the House's belief still at his back, he did not ask the Prior to open it.
known_facts.evidence: He did not ask.

known_facts.fact: He asked Maelis whether she had been down the undercroft stair, and she answered with a question.
known_facts.evidence: "Have you been down there?"

known_facts.fact: Since Maelis would not say whether she has been down the undercroft stair, he asked her to take him down it herself, on her count, with his hand on Wren's shoulder, stopping when she says stop.
known_facts.evidence: You won't tell me whether you've been down there

known_facts.fact: Told he has never waited for anything in his life, he said he is learning, from a good teacher who charges.
known_facts.evidence: I'm learning. I have a good teacher. She charges.

known_facts.fact: He read the flour by a lamp held low on the flags: no print in it or out, but a half-moon of frost glazed into it from the gap, every grain leaning toward the door.
known_facts.evidence: every grain of that glaze caught the light the same way, all of them leaning, as if the floor had been combed toward the door in the night

known_facts.fact: He believes something on the other side draws on the hall through the gap; the novice said breathed on, he said breathed in.
known_facts.evidence: "Breathed in," Darrow said.

known_facts.fact: He sent the lay brother from the fire and the young ones with the mallet to carry wood up the bell tower for Sister Pell instead.
known_facts.evidence: If you want something to carry, carry that.

known_facts.fact: Told he would want to be first down, he said he would be, on the Mender's count and with the Prior's key, and the last to arrive.
known_facts.evidence: On the Mender's count, with the Prior's key. I'll just be the last to arrive.

known_facts.fact: He would not let the House take the undercroft door off its pins: the Prior has the key, and the Mender has his word.
known_facts.evidence: Nobody touches this door without the Prior. She has the key, and the Mender has my word.

known_facts.fact: Asked by Maelis what he will do at the bottom of the stair, he said he will come back up, on this leg.
known_facts.evidence: He put his hand on the knee, the way you put a hand on a horse you are about to ask something of.

known_facts.fact: He told the kitchen novice the bet on NOBODY is that no other cot goes grey before the thaw, not who did it, and that nobody has won anything yet.
known_facts.evidence: The bet was no other cot goes grey before the thaw," he said. "Not who did it.

known_facts.fact: He told her to cross off a night every dawn there is no new grey blanket.
known_facts.evidence: Every dawn there's no new grey blanket, put a line through one.

known_facts.fact: He gave Rae the aye he lost to her on the gate wall: when he has been down the stair he will tell her what the cold does on the stone, plainly.
known_facts.evidence: When you've been down that stair, you'll tell me what the cold does on the stone. Plain. Not how you'd tell the House.

known_facts.fact: At the hour bell he said the oath aloud, the first words of it out of him since the river, and his throat did not shut on it.
known_facts.evidence: "Stone and Crown," he said, aloud, and the door was not there.

known_facts.fact: He said it for the lad, not for the Crown.
known_facts.evidence: "It wasn't for the Crown."

known_facts.fact: He takes the odd bells of the night for the lad, Hollis the even.
known_facts.evidence: You take the odd ones, Captain. I'll take the even.

known_facts.fact: He took the letters from the Confessor without letting his face show what the hand cost him.
known_facts.evidence: the way he had looked at a herald's writ across a table, with lords watching to see what it cost him. Then he took them.

known_facts.fact: The second letter asks: did you turn, tell me you did not turn toward the boy.
known_facts.evidence: Did you turn? Tell me you did not turn toward the boy.

known_facts.fact: The third, folded inside it, says: answer me, or I will come myself.
known_facts.evidence: Answer me, or I will come myself.

known_facts.fact: The letter is dated three days before the snow, before the list was read at Coldmere: Aldric knew where he was before the list.
known_facts.evidence: Calden, the third day before the snow.

known_facts.fact: He turned toward the boy in the river, on the left foot, and the knee went; but the warmth had gone out of him first, before the mare went down and before the boy.
known_facts.evidence: But the warmth had gone out of him first, halfway across, before any of it.

known_facts.fact: He believes Aldric, on the west bank and already climbing out, could not have seen which way he turned: somebody told him, and told it backwards.
known_facts.evidence: Somebody had told him, and told it backwards.

known_facts.fact: He reads the letter as written for two readers, with nothing a Confessor could use but its last line.
known_facts.evidence: It had been written for two readers.

known_facts.fact: He asked Hollis what became of the writ from the ford, which he never read on the bank.
known_facts.evidence: You broke the wax and held it out to me, and I didn't read it.

known_facts.fact: He did not ask to see the writ, and said he would like to be there when Hollis looks at the seal.
known_facts.evidence: "When you look," he said instead, "I'd like to be there."

known_facts.fact: He answered Aldric that he did turn toward Tobin, and the knee went, and he would turn again.
known_facts.evidence: Yes. I turned. I planted on a stone and turned toward Tobin, and the knee went, and I would turn again.

known_facts.fact: He wrote that the warmth went out of him first, before Thistle, the boy and the turn, and that whoever told Aldric was not there.
known_facts.evidence: The warmth went out of me first, halfway across, before Thistle went down, before the boy, before I turned. I was there. Whoever told you was not.

known_facts.fact: He wrote that he will not kneel, because he would be kneeling to the order told backwards.
known_facts.evidence: I will not kneel. Not for pride in the leg. Because I would be kneeling to that order told backwards.

known_facts.fact: He told Aldric he burned the first letter and nearly burned this one too so that Aldric would come, because he wants to see him and understand what he saw from the water.
known_facts.evidence: I burned your first. I nearly burned this one too, so that you would come. I want to see you that much.

known_facts.fact: He wrote Thistle's name and Tobin's in the letter.
known_facts.evidence: before Thistle went down, before the boy

known_facts.fact: He gave the letter through the bars unsealed and let the Confessor read it.
known_facts.evidence: folded once and not sealed

known_facts.fact: He wrote the letter twice over at a brazier that went out before he did.
known_facts.evidence: He had written it twice over at a brazier that went out before he did

known_facts.fact: On the warming-room stair he took his hand off the wall at the fifth step up, and the Mender put it back.
known_facts.evidence: took his wrist, and put his hand back flat on the stone

known_facts.fact: He had not asked the Mender that day; she said she would take him down anyway.
known_facts.evidence: he had not asked her today

known_facts.fact: He told the Prior he would look at the bottom and come back up on this leg, at the Mender's count.
known_facts.evidence: I look. Then I come back up it. On this leg, at her count.

known_facts.fact: He told Wren she has been good to him since the Steps, and that he has had her counting for him like a ledger.
known_facts.evidence: You've been good to me. Since the Steps, every day of it.

known_facts.fact: He knows the hand cut on the undercroft walls for the script that comes up over his palms; on the stone it does not read itself to him.
known_facts.evidence: He knew the hand.

known_facts.fact: He saw Wren read the words over the inner door straight off and stop, and said nothing.
known_facts.evidence: He closed his hand once on Wren's shoulder and left it there, and said nothing

known_facts.fact: He saw the frost beyond the pillars climb the far wall toward the vault, under the infirmary hall.
known_facts.evidence: It grew up the stone in feathers toward the vault

known_facts.fact: He kept his word to the Prior: he went down and came back up on his own leg.
known_facts.evidence: Then you've kept your word to me.

known_facts.fact: He did not say the mare's name in front of Wren; he has not said it since the Wend.
known_facts.evidence: He did not say the mare's name. He had not said it since the Wend

known_facts.fact: He told Rae plain what the cold does on the stone under the House, and not the way he would tell the House.
known_facts.evidence: So he told her, plain, the way she had asked it, and not the way he would have told the House.

known_facts.fact: He has a shirt, a stick, and a name on a Confessor's list that no dealer in the Lowmarch would take.
known_facts.evidence: a name on a Confessor's list that no dealer in the Lowmarch would take for a copper

known_facts.fact: He gave Rae his name at first light as surety for the grey mare, a captain's word for a dealer's debt.
known_facts.evidence: At first light he had given Rae his name for the mare, a captain's word to carry down to a dealer who would have no use for it

known_facts.fact: He knows the mortar round the thing in the alcove is new: pale, ungrained, with a trowel ridge and a thumbprint in it.
known_facts.evidence: pressed into it while it was wet, there was the print of a thumb

known_facts.fact: He knows someone came down and set the thing in the wall under the row, and went back up across a floor of flour that never showed a mark.
known_facts.evidence: Somebody had come down here in the dark with a trowel.

known_facts.fact: He reached for the thing in the alcove and Maelis took his wrist and stopped him.
known_facts.evidence: Maelis's fingers shut on his wrist from behind and took it back.

known_facts.fact: He watched walls go up at Edgemoor every summer of his boyhood and knows mortar at a week and at a year.
known_facts.evidence: He had watched a wall go up at Edgemoor every summer of his boyhood

known_facts.fact: He asked for a lamp of his own, oilcloth and the kitchen's pry bar to go back for it.
known_facts.evidence: "Then I'll need a lamp of my own," he said, to the hole. "Oilcloth. And the kitchen's pry bar."

known_facts.fact: He gave Maelis his word before going down: if she says up, it is up, at once.
known_facts.evidence: "If you say up, it's up."

known_facts.fact: He took the pry bar from Wren rather than let her do it: it is under the lad's cot, and his.
known_facts.evidence: "This is mine. It's under his cot."

known_facts.fact: He set the flat of the bar to the line where the mortar met the stone and leaned on it.
known_facts.evidence: He put the flat of the bar to the pale line where the mortar met the stone.

known_facts.fact: The cold from the stair has been in his hands since the night before and does not leave by the fire.
known_facts.evidence: It had come up the stair into his hands last night and had not left

known_facts.fact: He pried the mortar off the alcove in one piece: it was a lid pressed over a hole already there, with the thumbprint on its outside and a cast of the thing on its inside.
known_facts.evidence: It had never been part of the wall. It was a lid.

known_facts.fact: He saw the black thing in the back of the hole: glass-black like the chip from under the lad's tongue, the size of the last joint of a thumb, standing on end in the rock with frost running out of its foot in straight lines.
known_facts.evidence: The size of the last joint of a man's thumb. It did not sit on the rock; it stood up out of it a little, on end

known_facts.fact: He knows the thing came up in the House's own letter-satchel the day before the snow and was carried down and shut in the wall by hand.
known_facts.evidence: "It came up in the satchel," he said. "In the House's own bag, with the House's letters on top of it."

known_facts.fact: He stopped Wren from naming who carries the letters, down there.
known_facts.evidence: "Not down here." He said it quietly, and she stopped.

known_facts.fact: He put his right hand into the hole and could not pull the thing; the frost climbed his fingers past the second knuckle toward the wrist.
known_facts.evidence: The white passed the second knuckle and went on toward the wrist.

known_facts.fact: He stopped pulling and breathed as Maelis had taught him on the stair, and the frost stopped where it was.
known_facts.evidence: and breathed in, and did it again, and the white stopped where it was.

known_facts.fact: Holding it quietly he felt the black thing is one piece with the rock behind it, like a root with the ground, and that no hand or bar will take it out: only the lid came away.
known_facts.evidence: It had learned the wall. No hand would take it out of there, and no bar either

known_facts.fact: When Maelis said up he opened his fingers one at a time and brought the hand out open, and left the thing where it stood.
known_facts.evidence: he opened his fingers, one at a time, because they would only go one at a time, and brought the hand out of the hole open

known_facts.fact: The ends of his right-hand fingers came up white to the second joint; Maelis says he will have the use of the hand by the dawn bell and the ends of the fingers not for a week.
known_facts.evidence: "You'll have the use of it by the dawn bell," she said, flat, as if reading a knee.

known_facts.fact: He told Hollis first, on the floor, what is in the wall under the row and how it came up.
known_facts.evidence: He told Hollis there on the floor, low, with the Prior ten paces off and the whole row lit

known_facts.fact: He told the Prior everything in the chapel at the dawn bell, after the far cots' keeper, and said the order of telling was Hollis's asking.
known_facts.evidence: He told her it had been Hollis's asking that the keepers came first, because it was.

known_facts.fact: He knows there is a second way down to the undercroft: the old wine stair from the stores, opened by the stores key, which comes out behind a pillar at the kitchen end of the hall below.
known_facts.evidence: So there were two ways down.

known_facts.fact: He stopped Hollis with his full name and the voice from the ford, which he had not used since the water, and ordered him to sit.
known_facts.evidence: It came out of Darrow in the voice from the ford, the one that had put the Ninth into a line it did not want to hold.

known_facts.fact: He ordered the almoner to stay in the hall, eat, and keep the stores key on him, giving it to nobody, not the Prior, not Darrow himself.
known_facts.evidence: You'll keep the stores key on you and you'll give it to nobody, not the Prior, not me.

known_facts.fact: He stood up without remembering getting up, and the knee held.
known_facts.evidence: He did not remember getting up. The knee held.

known_facts.fact: He knows the hand on the almoner's letter: the same upright clerk's hand with a long-tailed y that wrote the direction on all three of his brother's letters, and not Aldric's own.
known_facts.evidence: He had seen it three times on the outside of folded paper, over blue wax, addressed to the Captain of the Ninth

known_facts.fact: He believes Marrant's whole method is the lever and that he has never needed a blade: the almoner's sister squeezed with a lock of hair.
known_facts.evidence: He did not need a blade. He had never needed one. The lever was the whole of his method

known_facts.fact: He asked Rae twice where she had seen the hand and she would not say.
known_facts.evidence: "I've seen that hand," she said, to the door.

known_facts.fact: The feeling is coming back into the ends of his right-hand fingers under the linen as a dull red heat; the cold let go of him a little in the night.
known_facts.evidence: a dull red heat in the ends of the right one's fingers where the feeling was coming back under the linen

known_facts.fact: He said the mare's name, Thistle, to Rae at the wicket, the first time he had said it since the river.
known_facts.evidence: He had not said it since the water. It came out of him rough

known_facts.fact: He chose not to ask Rae again about the hand on the letter, judging that asking would cost him the one question he had.
known_facts.evidence: It was the thing she would not give, and asking for it again would only cost him the one he had.

known_facts.fact: He sent his own name down for the mare because he will not have her stand in a dealer's byre under somebody else's word.
known_facts.evidence: I'm not having her stand in a dealer's byre under somebody else's word. If it has to be a bad word, it'll be mine.

known_facts.fact: He knows the Lowmarch's road song about a grey mare of Edgemoor; his men sang it worse than most; it is older than his mare and was true of her anyway.
known_facts.evidence: It had not been written about his mare; it was older than both of them. It had been true of her anyway.

known_facts.fact: He asked Sister Pell what the bell says at dusk, and when she lost his words in the bad light he said them again plain, to her face, without the joke.
known_facts.evidence: He turned so the window was on his face and said it again, plain, and left off the joke he had been going to put on the end of it

known_facts.fact: He said the four lines of the dusk verse back to her and stopped on the third, What climbed, we keep.
known_facts.evidence: got as far as the third line and stopped on it.

known_facts.fact: He owes Sister Pell a dusk under the tower, in the court, saying the lines with the strokes where she can see his mouth from the window.
known_facts.evidence: Dusk. Under the tower, in the court, where I can see your mouth from the window. You'll say them with the strokes

known_facts.fact: He kept his wrapped right hand inside his shirt when she spoke of the bell poured again with its own crack in it.
known_facts.evidence: Darrow's right hand was inside his shirt, where the linen was. He left it there.

known_facts.fact: He told Wren plainly that she did well to catch the lock of hair at the gate before it reached the slush.
known_facts.evidence: "You caught it," he said. "The hair. At the gate.

known_facts.fact: He lowered himself into the straw by the post with the bad leg out straight, and made sure it was not kneeling.
known_facts.evidence: It was not kneeling. He made sure of that.

known_facts.fact: He held out his good hand to the hound and left it there when she bit it.
known_facts.evidence: every year of the Lances in him said take the hand back, and he left it where it was.

known_facts.fact: When the hound let go and stood shaking over the bitten hand, his wrapped hand came toward her on its own and he put it back on his knee.
known_facts.evidence: The other hand, the wrapped one, had come an inch off his knee toward her without being asked, and he put it back.

known_facts.fact: The hound bit his left hand through the skin at the thumb, and he did not pull it away.
known_facts.evidence: the meat of the thumb, a hard clamp and a tooth through the skin

known_facts.fact: The hound lay down with her splinted leg across his boot and slept, and he did not move his foot.
known_facts.evidence: put the splinted leg across his boot, and laid her head on her own paws, and shut her eyes.

known_facts.fact: The kennel-master gave him until the grey cloaks are gone: if the hound is eating from somebody's hand by then, she gets the meat.
known_facts.evidence: If she's eating from somebody's hand by then, I'll find her the meat.

known_facts.fact: He eased his boot out from under the sleeping hound a finger's width at a time and left her in the run; she watched the foot go and did not lift her head.
known_facts.evidence: she opened one eye and watched the foot go and did not lift her head

known_facts.fact: He let Brother Anselm bind the bitten hand, and noticed the almoner's hands were steady.
known_facts.evidence: His own hands were steady. Darrow had not expected that.

known_facts.fact: He asked Anselm what his sister's mark is and why she is the brave one, and promised him nothing.
known_facts.evidence: "Brother. Your sister's mark. The one nobody else has."

known_facts.fact: He saw the half-ring of small white marks on the farrier's right hand, the size of a hound's jaw, and said it had teeth in it; the farrier said it had a burn in it.
known_facts.evidence: "It's got teeth in it."

known_facts.fact: He stood in the smoke at the fair while the Ninth's brand, a gate, two posts and a bar, went onto sixty horses.
known_facts.evidence: he had stood in the smoke at the fair while it went onto sixty horses, the greys fighting the men who held them.

known_facts.fact: He caught the remade cup against his chest with both bad hands and swore.
known_facts.evidence: Darrow caught it against his chest with both bad hands, and swore

known_facts.fact: He is carrying the farrier's remade cup up to Hollis: ten steps, not nine, and where it bites goes back to the farrier.
known_facts.evidence: He puts it on, he stands, he takes ten steps, not nine, and he tells you where it bites, and you tell me, not him.

known_facts.fact: He said the four lines of the dusk verse aloud under the tower, with the strokes, where Sister Pell could see him from the window, and did not stop on the third line this time.
known_facts.evidence: He said the third line and did not stop on it this time, and the bell went over it.

known_facts.fact: He heard the Confessor name his price: the almoner sent down, and two names come off his paper, whose unsaid.
known_facts.evidence: Send the almoner down to me, and two names come off my paper. I'll not say whose. You'll know whose.

known_facts.fact: He read the Confessor with the script and found no lie in him: Marrant means the two names and can afford to, because they come off his paper only, and his paper is not the only paper on the road.
known_facts.evidence: He meant the two names. He could afford to mean them: they would come off his paper, and his paper was not the only paper on the road.

known_facts.fact: He told the cot what he had read under the price: that the man meant every word, and that meaning it cost him nothing.
known_facts.evidence: that the man meant every word, and that meaning it cost him nothing.

known_facts.fact: He told the Confessor he would have an answer at the dawn bell.
known_facts.evidence: "You'll have an answer at the dawn bell," Darrow said.

known_facts.fact: He refused Anselm's offer to go down to the Confessor, by his full name, and said it is not on the table.
known_facts.evidence: "You'll not go down. That isn't on the table, and I'll not have you put it there again."

known_facts.fact: He asked each of them what they would do with the price and said he is thinking of using the letters.
known_facts.evidence: "That's what I'm thinking," he said. "The letters."

known_facts.fact: He said that if a letter down were caught, the next letter up would come without the hook in her M.
known_facts.evidence: "Then the next letter up comes without the hook in her M," Darrow said.

known_facts.fact: He sat on his own cot with the gap between them, as he has since the night the lid came off.
known_facts.evidence: He sat on his own cot with the width of the gap between them, the way he had sat since the night the lid came off

known_facts.fact: He said he would have told Anselm every word without Hollis's price, because he will not have one more man in the House sent somewhere on a paper he has not read.
known_facts.evidence: Hollis made it his price, and I'd have done it without him, so hear it as mine. I'll not have one more man in this House sent somewhere on a paper he hasn't read.

known_facts.fact: He told Anselm he has not stopped seeing the trowel in his hand, and that he knows the shape of being lied to by a paper, having been sent into a river on one.
known_facts.evidence: I've not stopped seeing the trowel in your hand, and I'll not pretend I have.

known_facts.fact: He said Anselm gets every word not because he has earned it but because the other way is the clerk's.
known_facts.evidence: Not because you've earned it. Because the other way is his.

known_facts.fact: He gave the letter a purpose for the sister, the one he said he cares about: to learn where she is kept, since a clerk who answers a brother's question about her shawl will name the place or lie about it, and either is more than they have.
known_facts.evidence: For her, one thing, and it's the one I care about. We don't know where she is.

known_facts.fact: He refused the trade because it would send Anselm down into their hands and get the sister nothing, and said so though he had read no lie in the Confessor.
known_facts.evidence: The other one, the trade, sends you down the Steps into their hands and gets her nothing. I'll not take it.

known_facts.fact: He told Anselm plainly that if the letter is caught she pays for it, and that it is a better risk than another month of doing nothing, and that Anselm could refuse it.
known_facts.evidence: It's a better risk than leaving her where she is and doing nothing, which is what I've done for a month. That's my judgment. You can refuse it.

known_facts.fact: He read the letter as it was written and changed no word of it: it said everything he had asked and none of it in his words, and was better for that.
known_facts.evidence: It said everything he had asked it to say and none of it in the words he had given, and it was better for that

known_facts.fact: He said yes to Anselm's vow to go down to the bell at Coldmere when it is over and ask aloud what was done with his sister.
known_facts.evidence: "You keep saying that."

known_facts.fact: Through the kennel grate he felt the same cold as the stone in the wall under the row and the black glass under Benedek's tongue.
known_facts.evidence: the stone in the wall under the row, the black glass under Benedek's tongue, the cold that a hand remembers

known_facts.fact: He named the grey hound Ash, for the brazier gone grey before the dawn bell, when no kennel word would call her off.
known_facts.evidence: there was one left in his mouth from the morning, from the brazier gone grey before the dawn bell

known_facts.fact: He played the knucklebones left-handed, the right's fingertips still wrapped and the left thumb bound, and lost at the threes.
known_facts.evidence: On the threes the thrown bone came down past his knuckles and he grabbed for it and got a handful of blanket.

known_facts.fact: He broke his nose at fourteen on a well-windlass at home, letting the bucket down without a hand on the crank to show a girl from the lower holding, and looking at her when she smiled.
known_facts.evidence: "A well-windlass," he said. "At home. I was fourteen.

known_facts.fact: He was standing still when the crank came round.
known_facts.evidence: "I was standing still."

known_facts.fact: As a boy of eleven he had walked at a horse's head since before he could argue, the way a horse-breeder's son is raised in the Edgemoor hills.
known_facts.evidence: since before he could argue

known_facts.fact: He got onto the bay by going sideways into the place it had just left instead of backward, and up the rail to be higher than its eye.
known_facts.evidence: higher than the bay's eye

known_facts.fact: His father, who said nothing about most things, opened the gate for him without a word.
known_facts.evidence: as he said nothing about most things

relationships.label: his Mender
relationships.note: She tied the Binding with a strand of his own sinew and emberthread, reads the Knots with two fingers and her eyes shut, has told him fifteen times he may not go down the Steps, and it is she who will make him be honest, later, about how much he loved the charge.

relationships.label: of the Sixth Lance, on the next cot
relationships.note: He waved the writ at Darrow on the west bank and told him his head was not as fast as his feet; lost his right leg above the knee at the ford, cursed Darrow among many others on the carts north, and snores on his right at Saint Ysolde's, second on the list where Wren, asked who was first, only looked at Darrow. At the gate Hollis saw him move at his name, told him nobody else had, and called him Captain when he gave his name at the bars.

relationships.label: the girl with the ledger who counted him up the Steps
relationships.note: She counted the steps aloud beside his litter and would not let him say she had missed one; it was she who brought word of the grey cloaks, and who looked at him when Hollis asked whose name was first. After he gave his name at the bars she made him count lamps while she told him how stupid it was, and wrote down his promise to tell her first next time.

relationships.label: knighted the same morning
relationships.note: Squires together, knighted the same morning; at the ford Aldric told him to ride wider and seemed about to say more, and Darrow saw his horse already turned on the west bank; Darrow believes it was Aldric's hand that wrote his name first on the Confessors' list.

relationships.label: the youngest of the Ninth
relationships.note: Nineteen, who sang badly and constantly; when Tobin went under his own horse in the current, Darrow came off his mare and turned toward him, and that turn is where the knee went.

relationships.label: the woman who pulled him out
relationships.note: She looked at him alone across the water before the charge and called something the river took; afterward she hauled him to the east bank, made him look at what the Wend was carrying, and was gone when he turned back; he did not see her again for a long time.

relationships.label: the carter who drove him the last of the road
relationships.note: She talked to her oxen and not to him, looked at his leg once like a cracked wheel, and said one thing to him all day; seven weeks after the Binding he knew her cart at the winch-house from the window, and Wren says it was she who heard the list read and climbed through the night to bring it up.
